before: Changing a content control tag, alias, or lock replaced the property element with a new identity. Two concurrent writers each removed the old element and inserted their own, so the merged control held two w:tag or w:alias children, every remote apply failed known-node validation, and both sessions entered error.
after: An existing property element keeps its identity and only its w:val attribute changes; an unchanged value writes nothing. Missing properties are still added and removed properties are still dropped.
reason: The writer emits an existing setAttribute on an existing identity instead of a child splice. Unchanged provider readers already replicate attributes as registers. No shared schema, protocol, journal, or materialization rule changes.
